note:
External reference geometry for blind benchmarks. Nothing here is committed: these are third-party artifacts, and AGENTS.md forbids putting them in this repository. ARCHITECTURE.md 16.6 is the rule they follow instead -- a corpus that stays external and is referenced by stable identity and hash. `tools/corpus.py` fetches them and verifies every digest.

QUESTION MATERIAL LIVES IN `request` AND NOWHERE ELSE. Everything outside a `request` block -- this note, an id, a path, a url, a source's `why` -- is for a maintainer and a grader, and may say whatever it needs to. Everything inside one is handed to a generator that writes the benchmark question, and `corpus.request_view()` is the only door to it: two keys, types pinned, `purpose` scanned for any numeral or number-word, `interfaces` restricted to `request_vocabulary` below. Two earlier versions put that rule in a test instead, as a pattern over the committed text; the first was broken twelve ways in one review pass and the second nineteen, including by moving the measurement into a JSON number, into a dict key, and into the entry id.

The interface claims are read off the vendor's own filenames and Voron 2's published hardware list. They are not measured, and no benchmark scores them.
request_vocabulary_note: The declared disclosure: every dimension this corpus gives away in a question, listed in one place. A term here is admissible because it is on this list, not because it looks harmless -- that is the difference between a whitelist and the exemption list this replaced. Growing it means editing this file and the test that pins it, so a dimension cannot start being disclosed without somebody saying so.

voron2.why: Real functional printed parts designed around standard hardware -- M3 fasteners, 2020 aluminium extrusion, MGN9 linear rails, GT2 belts. That matters for a blind benchmark: the question can state what the part has to interface with, in the vocabulary a person would actually use, without stating the part's own geometry. This field is not question material and is never handed to a generator; the vocabulary a question may use is `request_vocabulary`, above.

request.purpose: Holds a deck panel against an extrusion so the panel cannot lift.
Holds a linear rail true to an extrusion while it is bolted down.
Retains a bottom panel in the slot of an extrusion.
Clamps the end of a toothed belt so it cannot pull through.
